title: Guided onboarding: in-console checklist MVP (scope, milestones, and acceptance criteria)
creator: Alex Martinez
project: Guided onboarding + First production launch checklist
description:
## Summary
Ship an in-product onboarding checklist in Redwood Console for Hosted API that guides new tenants from signup -> first successful API call (TTFS) -> first production traffic (TTFP). The checklist is backed by a progress-tracking service and reliable onboarding event instrumentation (server-side emission preferred), and is paired with updated docs/quickstarts and a Support triage playbook.

This is the top-level PM tracking issue for MVP scope, milestones, and launch acceptance criteria.

## Goals (MVP)
1) Reduce median time from signup -> first successful API call (TTFS).
2) Reduce median time from signup -> first production traffic (TTFP).
3) Increase activation/retention by making required steps explicit and discoverable in Console.
4) Reduce top onboarding-related support tickets (401/403 auth mistakes, rate-limit surprises, streaming disconnect confusion, billing/usage dashboard mismatches).

## Non-goals (explicitly out of scope for MVP)
- Full in-product guided tours / walkthrough overlays.
- Private deployment onboarding wizard (VPC/on-prem), beyond ensuring the system is extensible.
- Automated remediation suggestions / “fix it for me” actions (tracked as follow-ons).

## Target persona(s)
- Primary: software engineers / ML engineers integrating Hosted API into an application for the first time.
- Secondary: engineering managers / platform engineers who need a lightweight production-readiness checklist for internal go-live.

## MVP scope
### Console (UI/UX)
- Checklist entry point in Console + persistent checklist state per tenant.
- Step list with statuses (Not started / In progress / Complete / Needs attention where applicable).
- Step detail view with:
  - What this step means
  - Acceptance criteria
  - Deep links into relevant Console pages and canonical docs
  - Lightweight troubleshooting hints for common failures
- Feature-flag gated exposure + cohorting rules; kill switch.
- Admin/support override tooling (mark step complete/reset) with audit trail and strict permissions.

### Platform/Telemetry
- Onboarding event schema v1 and server-side emission points:
  - API key created
  - First successful 2xx request (by endpoint category)
  - First streaming response established
  - First 401/403, first 429, streaming disconnect patterns (for “needs attention” / troubleshooting context)
  - Usage dashboard viewed (optional, if emitted via server-side page view tracking)
  - Model pinned / fallback policy configured (as control plane config events)
- Progress service:
  - Event ingestion (write-only internal)
  - Idempotency + out-of-order handling
  - Monotonic step transitions (avoid regressions)
  - API for Console to fetch step state + computed progress
- KPI dashboards:
  - TTFS + TTFP trendlines (median/p75)
  - Step completion funnel and drop-off
  - Cohort filters (region, SDK, acquisition channel where available)
  - Data freshness checks + regression alerts

### SDKs + examples (aligned guidance)
- “Production-safe defaults” guidance for retries/timeouts and streaming reconnect patterns (language parity as best-effort).
- Update snippets/quickstarts to reflect checklist steps and reduce top failure modes.

### Docs
- Canonical checklist doc mirrored with Console steps.
- Tighten docs IA so each checklist step has a single canonical target page (and redirects).

## Success metrics
See metric definitions and validation plan in PM-751.
- Primary:
  - Median TTFS down (target: -20% vs baseline within 30 days of rollout)
  - Median TTFP down (target: -15% vs baseline within 45 days of rollout; expected lag)
- Secondary:
  - Funnel completion: % tenants reaching “First successful request” within 24h
  - Reduction in onboarding-related Support tickets per 100 new tenants (target: -15% within 45 days)
  - Increase in “streaming established” adoption for chat workloads (directional)

## Rollout plan (MVP)
See PM-768 for cohorting/killswitch details.
- Phase 0: internal dogfood + test tenants; validate event ordering/idempotency.
- Phase 1: limited cohort rollout (new self-serve Hosted API tenants only).
- Phase 2: expand to larger cohort; monitor KPI deltas + ticket volume; iterate.

## Milestones
- M0: Discovery complete
  - Checklist content outline agreed (DevEx + PM + Design)
  - Event schema v1 reviewed (Telemetry + Security)
- M1: MVP feature-flagged end-to-end
  - Events emitted -> progress service -> Console renders step states
  - Docs + quickstarts updated and linked
- M2: Dogfood feedback addressed
  - Fix major UX clarity issues, deep-link gaps, and state regression bugs
- M3: Limited cohort rollout + KPI dashboard live
  - Data quality checks passing; regression alerts enabled
- M4: Support readiness
  - Triage playbook + macros updated; admin override available

## Acceptance criteria (go/no-go)
### Functionality
- Checklist is visible in Console for flagged tenants and hidden for control cohorts.
- Step states persist and do not regress due to out-of-order events (monotonic transitions).
- Core steps can be completed end-to-end using at least one official quickstart (Python or TypeScript) without needing Support.
- Deep links:
  - Each step has at least 1 deep link to the relevant Console page OR canonical docs page.
  - No broken links; redirects verified.

### Telemetry + data quality
- Events conform to onboarding-event-schema-v1 and are PII-free.
- Event ingestion is resilient (idempotent; handles retries and duplicates).
- KPI dashboards show:
  - TTFS and step funnel populated for new cohorts
  - Data freshness < 2 hours lag for the funnel dashboards (excluding backfill jobs)
- Backfill job provides baseline TTFS/TTFP for pre-rollout comparison.

### Performance / reliability
- Checklist API P95 latency for state fetch < 250ms under expected Console usage.
- Feature flag kill switch can disable checklist rendering without impacting core Console pages.

### Support readiness
- Support can interpret checklist state (doc + internal macro).
- Support/admin override actions are permissioned and audited.

## Open questions / decisions needed
- Final definition of “First successful request” (endpoint scope, excluding health checks, retries) tracked in PM-751.
- Which “needs attention” states to surface in MVP vs keep as passive troubleshooting content.
- Whether usage-dashboard views should be counted as a step completion or remain informational.

## Notes
- We are optimizing for reliable server-side eventing to reduce SDK/version variance. Client hints (e.g., user-agent tags) are permitted but should not be required for core step completion.
- Checklist copy must remain concise; detail should live in linked docs. Console should focus on “what to do next” and “what good looks like.”

2025-04-08 (Dev Patel): Support readiness: admin override is required for MVP rollout. Without it, we can’t unblock customers if state gets stuck. Please ensure audit logging shows who changed what and why.

acceptance_criteria: Checklist is feature-flagged and can be enabled per cohort; kill switch works.
Progress service stores and returns step state; Console renders correct statuses for flagged tenants.
Events emitted from gateway/control plane conform to schema v1; idempotent ingestion; monotonic transitions prevent regressions.
KPI dashboard for funnel + TTFS/TTFP is live with data freshness checks and regression alerts.
Docs/quickstarts are updated and linked from each checklist step; links verified and owned in docs IA.
Support playbook exists and Support has admin override tooling with audited actions.
